prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its biologically active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: I keep the same configuration after the full first-round exchange. The case for B041 is the arc from gut-hormone physiology to a drug class: the incretin effect and secretion of GLP-1 in humans, identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form, the peptide's actions on islets, appetite and gastric emptying, and then independent randomized outcome trials showing glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit. The discovery began in basic hormone biology, which fits the prize's remit, and it has been confirmed over decades by several groups and several drugs. Maturity is not in doubt and waiting adds little. Holst, Mojsov and Drucker each stand for a distinct step that had to exist before any analogue could be designed, and a single-achievement prize keeps the citation about discovery and keeps the three-person limit honest.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and round 1 did not remove it. Knudsen's long-acting analogue design is what made the marketed drugs work, and the three-name limit leaves her out. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and nobody in the committee, including me, can settle it from the supplied material. Habener and other early contributors fall outside the credited list. If the committee decides that the drug-design step is the achievement, my trio is the wrong one and I would want an explicit argument about which name gives way rather than a default exclusion of Mojsov. A secondary concern is that a prize with three physiology names and a product-side omission may be read as undervaluing the medicinal chemistry. I accept that cost, but I do not regard it as free.

responses.point: A configuration split between physiology and translation may be fairer if the committee judges that the drug-design step must be honoured, with Knudsen possibly in a separate part.
responses.response: I considered this seriously, since a second part is the only way to name Knudsen without cutting a physiology name. I do not support it. A second part for drug design would have to share the three-person cap, which means cutting B041 to two names, and I see no documented basis in the supplied record for deciding which of Holst, Drucker or Mojsov is least central. A two-part split would also pair two halves of one achievement, not two distinct achievements. I keep the single physiology prize and state Knudsen's exclusion as a cost.

responses.point: B041 rewards the discovery rather than the product, but a prize heavily weighted to translational success could look like a prize for commercial impact; he would reopen the trio only if the citation were framed around the therapies.
responses.response: I agree, and that is the reason I keep the citation about physiology and the active form of the peptide, with the therapies mentioned only as consequence. Our positions are close. Where I differ slightly is that I would not treat Knudsen as a purely commercial contributor: her work was scientific medicinal chemistry. It is, however, a later step in the chain, and I would keep it outside the discovery being credited. I also note your ranking of B035 behind B030 and B023. I accept that on clinical grounds, though I still keep B035 as my second alternative because its attribution is cleaner.

responses.point: CAR-T is equally mature with a clearer concept-to-clinic story for the credited names, so waiting on B041 would cost little if the credit dispute cannot be resolved.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument against my position, and I take it seriously. CAR-T limited to June and Sadelain is the most defensible second achievement, and Eshhar's absence is a real gap. But I do not think the GLP-1 credit dispute is unresolvable. It is a question of how to word the citation, not of whether the discovery is complete. B041 has all six first-place votes and the larger and more broadly confirmed clinical effect, and I see no reason to defer it. I also note that I have co-authored with you, as disclosed, and that this does not affect my view of B041 or B030.

responses.point: A single-achievement prize keeps the citation about physiology, and a two-part prize would require cutting B041 to two names.
responses.response: I agree with your arithmetic and with the preference it leads to. The only two-part version I could defend would be B041 with two names plus B030 with June and Sadelain, which requires dropping Drucker, Holst or Mojsov without a documented reason. That is a worse outcome than leaving CAR-T for another year. I also hold B035 as an alternative for a mechanistic prize, and I am more cautious than you about calling its translational links secure. The links to disease are still largely associative.

responses.point: Near-unanimity may reflect shared salience of the weight-loss drugs rather than careful credit analysis, and the omission of the drug-design step may read as incomplete.
responses.response: That concern is fair and I tried to test it. The weight-loss salience is real, but the case does not depend on it: GLP-1 physiology and the active peptide were established before obesity was an indication, and the clinical evidence comes from independent trials across type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular and renal outcomes. The incompleteness risk is real and I would name it openly in the committee's discussion of the citation. I do not think it requires adding Knudsen at the cost of one of the three discovery names, and I would still not use Mojsov's contested priority as a reason to remove her without evidence.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and the roles of Habener and other early contributors cannot be resolved from the supplied evidence, and I would change my allocation only if documented evidence made one of the three names clearly less central.
Whether the committee prefers to frame the citation around physiology or around the drugs, which would change who is central.
Whether B030 for June and Sadelain should be paired with B041 in a later year, and how to treat the chimeric receptor originators outside the credited names.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile. Optogenetics (B039) is adjacent to my field, but my profile records no involvement with its credited names. My documented co-authorship in spatial transcriptomics and brain atlases, including works with Rickard Sandberg, concerns work outside the shortlist. Nothing in round 1 changes this disclosure.
